chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: Benny Carter and the 1930 Henderson band; tuba and bass together
summary: Hearing Henderson's band with Carter in 1930, Jackson names the whole lineup and says bands like Kirby's and McKinney's used both tuba and bass.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: But what about -- When did Bennie Carter come into this?
Bennie Carter -- the first time I heard Bennie Carter was with Fletcher Henderson.
Alto sax?
That's right. 1930 I heard that band. That was the most fantastic band I had ever heard in my life.
What band was that?
Fletcher Henderson.
And Bennie Carter was playing with him?

He was playing alto. He and Harvey Boone and Coleman Hawkins was the saxophone section. Trumpets was Russell Smith and Bobby Stark and Rex Stewart. And the trombones was Jimmy Harrison and Claude Jones. Now, what more do you want after that?
No more.
John Kirby was on bass and Clarence Holiday, Billie Holiday's father, was on guitar. And Walter Johnson was on drums.
Right, Walter Johnson.
The greatest rhythm section that you would ever want to hear in life. You talk about togetherness --
That should have been great. Was John Kirby playing tuba with him?
Both.
Both tuba and bass?
Oh, yes, he used both. He had both on the bandstand. Billy Taylor used to have both on the bandstand, too.
Uh-huh.
Sure, they'd use like -- mostly they'd use the bass fiddle for the extreme swing numbers and they used the tuba for the pretty numbers, you see.
The tuba hadn't completely left --
Oh, no.
-- then, because that's when I came in.
No, they hadn't left.
In the thirties they hadn't completely left.
Oh, no. Uh-uh, no.
Completely left the bandstand.
Uh-uh, no, because I have records of McKinney's Cottonpickers where they use both.
